[Discussion] How come that some delayed games turn out great because of it and some turn out worse because of the delay?

The games which turn out great are delayed because the developers refuse to release an unfinished product.

The games which turn out to be garbage are probably projects gong wrong and not even playable at the deadline. So they just try to make something sellable with the remaining budget ASAP.
If Goldeneye 007 was delayed for a few years, how would its reception have changed?

If it were too long since the film, they'd have had to change the title. As long as the platform is still selling strong and there are no technologically more advanced games I doubt it would have hurt the reception much. It sure would have cost more to develop though.

Too long delays can make a game outdated before it's even released. That's why they had to change the engine multiple times in Duke Nukem Whenever and this caused further delays.
Now imagine if Starcraft: Ghost would be released.

It really does have to do with the studio, and how development is going. A delay to tidy things up and make sure the game is right is typically a good thing, but when the delays are due to worse issues (ex: Game nowhere near done, core mechanics fundamentally broken, etc), it tends to lead to crap.

Positive Example: The Witcher 3. CD Projekt knew the game wasn't fully read for prime-time, so took some extra time to polish things as well as optimized, rather than release a sub-optimal game. They were upfront about it and kept the community in the loop.

Negative Example: Duke Nukem Forever. It got passed around several developers/studios, had to be re-written at least once as it got dated. It seems the entire development process was an unorganized mess. At the end they just had to push something out to try and get some money as the costs at that point had to be kind of insane.

Tons of factors. Sometimes a project will get killed and picked up by another studio, and wind up with different publishers.

Sometimes a studio doesn't have the creative control that they'd like and end up with a lot of pressure from their producers, so they end up in a pissing match. Eventually they build a monument to compromise.

I think it comes down to the reasons for delay.

The games that come out as an ungodly mess always suffer from chasing new technology or feature creep. Insecure about how their game is going to do compared to what's coming out, they try to upgrade their tech or cram in new gameplay, which delays the project. During the delays, they get leapfrogged again, forcing them to upgrade and cram again. Repeat until a demoralized team and high turnover eventually forces management to just release what they've got.

The games that seem to have benefitted from delays are ones where a clear vision is being adhered to. The team isn't chasing after what others are doing, but instead are drawing on their own sources of inspiration. They just need more time to really nail down the details of their vision. Get the mechanics to feel right, and the world to hang together properly.

I will say though, not every game neatly falls into one or the other. From what I've heard Bioshock Infinite was a little bit of both. It underwent constant massive redesigns, that came from a good place, but that still had a demoralizing effect on the team. However, I think the game still stands on it's own perfectly well due to not chasing the competition and instead sticking to it's own vision.
Delay wouldn't hurt great game and won't help crappy game neither.

I really hope fallout 4 won't get delayed but if it needs to be delayed until December, or 2016, because of playability or content issues etc. I wouldn't really be upset.

The way I see it, delays are almost always a good thing. A developer is actively choosing to postpone making money on the game, besides the pay from development, which if I understand right, is usually contractual and time limited so a delay causes serious problems.

I can't think of any games made worse than release delays tbh. Games that fall off the radar then show up and look/play horrible compared to previously? That's much more common.

Is it possible that the way we understand how Karma works may be wrong and the universe rewards some people for doing bad things?

It depends upon one's perspective. Sometimes the world seems to reward the power hungry, the egotistical, the money grubbers, but often these people's pride and egomania come back to bite them, Ex. Steve Jobs and his pancreatic cancer treatment of fruits

Karma existing is an assumption based on no evidence, but rather "that'd be nice if the universe worked that way."

So yes, it's equally plausible to assume there exists a "counter-karma" so to speak, that works in the opposite manner.

On a merely empirical level, there are plenty of examples of people being rewarded for doing bad things, or not facing retribution for their slights.

Yeah this is the correct answer that I came here to say. Karma is an imagined construct that human beings invented, like heaven and hell, ghosts and demons and angels. There are plenty of people who get away with murders and ripping others off.

Now, if we consider re-incarnation, one life's karma contributing to the formation of the next life and because you did bad in life 1 you come back as a urinary tract bacterium, this is obviously something we can't prove or disprove but it's likely that this is also make-believe.
I don't think there is any ethereal karma rewarding some actions over others. What actions are or are not rewarded is up to the rest of us.

In the notion of "Karma rewards those who reward themselves" then yes. If you do what you feel is right, for you, or you do what you feel is right for somebody else. Either way, you are doing what you feel is the right thing to do, then Karma will ultimately reward you for your actions. You make your own Karma. It really is in direct response to the actions you've taken.

Did you shit on a coworker in order to get ahead? That was a shitty thing you did but the Karma of the affect is that you got ahead in your career. Now you make more money, are in a better position and feel more secure. That is your karma for the decisions you've made. The person who got shit on? Well, depending on what they do about that, that will make up the extent of their karma. If they do nothing but pine and moan on about how the world is always unfair to them and shits on them, their karma will take a downward path, if they say "Fuck it, I'm going to figure out how to overcome this, they will figure out a way to shit on the next person, or lift themselves up out of what just happened and see to it that, that moment doesn't become the cascade in a long line of shit related moments all trailing from one incident.

The karma is not set, there is no karma but that which we make for ourselves.

"The way we understand how karma works" is assuming that karma works. It is a word for an invisible device that is only supported by confirmation bias, but has no real grounds in reality.

If you're looking for an invisible device that rewards people based on their actions, then good luck, because that is about as good as you can get. Instead, I find it liberating to not believe in invisible things that are impossible to prove.
